html:
SMTO-CTX-0021 — SMTO couldn't measure the size of a request to the AI model

GUID: ca1f8e33-b7a3-45cc-9310-de9f12df41b9
Slug: tokenizer-response-invalid
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: ctx

What happened

  • Before asking the AI model, SMTO asks the model server how big the request is. The server's answer was unreadable. This message is about counting only; it does not mean the model answered.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, find the model you use (for example Main), and select Check saved model. This tests whether the model server answers SMTO correctly right now.
  2. If the check reports a problem, ask the person who runs the model server to confirm it is running and up to date. An unreadable size answer usually comes from a model server that is misconfigured or a version SMTO doesn't support.
  3. Once the check passes, open the stopped task, see which steps it already finished, and then ask SMTO only for the work that is still missing. This message doesn't show how far the task got, so checking first avoids doing finished work twice.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model reports its checks as passing and the task continues getting model replies.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the model server or SMTO. Don't remove saved tasks or turn off security checks to make the model look healthy.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The model endpoint's tokenizer returned a measurement response SMTO could not parse, so exact input-token counting for the request failed before inference.

What this means

  • This retained tokenizer-response identity denotes an unsupported measurement shape; its source-message export remains, but no direct current producer was found. This identity remains for historical or external payloads; no live direct producer was found. Historical facts, including whether inference began, must come from the saved occurrence.

Why this can happen

  • This retained tokenizer-response identity denotes an unsupported measurement shape; its source-message export remains, but no direct current producer was found.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the recorded tokenization stage and any retained measurement provenance; avoid reconstructing a precise count from an old error label.

How to fix it

  • No current code raises this error ID directly: today an unreadable tokenizer response is recorded as the invalid_tokenizer_response diagnostic and the client stops using exact counts for that run (openai_compat/context.py). For a recorded occurrence, check that the configured OpenAI-compatible server's tokenizer endpoint returns an integer token count, verify it with Check saved model in Settings > Setup > Model routing, and take historical facts, including whether inference began, from the saved error record rather than assuming a model response.
  • Check the served tokenizer endpoint and model profile compatibility. Restore valid token measurements before submitting inference; do not report a model response that never occurred.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The active tokenizer boundary supplies a supported measurement before inference is admitted.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • This identity remains for historical or external payloads; no live direct producer was found. Historical facts, including whether inference began, must come from the saved occurrence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
